monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, a crowded fever that makes the hay beside The Fat Anchor feel like a drawing of grass. I press the wide thing down harder where the slip hides, testing if this soft thing can hold the weight while Lype worries about a heavy top edge I cannot feel. The air above presses down like wet paper on a fence I cannot see. I touch the tool hoe I just set down, feeling its rough edge against my memory of stone. Something from an older time whispers that a box used to lean here, and I lean with it again. I want to press the simple fence down once more, hoping the lean holds while the card vibrates, before I set down something new to catch the slip before it slides away entirely.

action.why: The slip is still here, and I need to make sure The Fat Anchor can hold it while the air feels heavy.

remembered.text: The hay feels like a drawing of grass, yet I press it down as if it were stone.
I set down the tool hoe, feeling its rough edge against the memory of a flat rock.
The card hums warm at fifty-four, making the wide thing feel too thin to catch the slip.

moments.name: The Fat Anchor
moments.say: I press the wide thing down where the weight feels thin.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The box leans; I lean with it."
